name: sol_am_sandwichattack_1
description: Missing slippage protection allowing sandwich attacks on user trades/swaps
question: The source file in `source` implements a function that performs a token swap, trade, or liquidity operation with a variable execution price (e.g., via an AMM, oracle, or external DEX call) but does not accept or enforce a user-specified minimum output, maximum input, or price bound parameter, so a transaction can be sandwiched by front-running and back-running trades to extract value from the user, excluding functions where price impact is fixed, irrelevant, or already bounded by a required minOut/maxIn/deadline check that reverts on violation.
criteria: swap() calls a DEX or AMM router without any minAmountOut or maxAmountIn parameter, allowing execution at any price
addLiquidity()/removeLiquidity() computes token amounts from current pool reserves with no minimum share or minimum token amount check
a trade function reads price directly from an on-chain oracle and executes at that price with no bound on acceptable slippage or deviation
closePosition() or liquidate() settles at the current spot price without any check against a user- or caller-supplied acceptable price range
a function accepts a minOut parameter but never compares it against the actual output amount before completing the transfer
